title: VS Code
summary: A desktop editor built on Electron with a multi-process architecture: the UI renderer stays responsive while extensions run in a separate extension host, language intelligence comes from out-of-process language servers (LSP), and remote development splits the editor from the machine that runs the code.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: Open folders, edit files, search across files, integrated terminal, debugging, Git
Language features for hundreds of languages: completion, go-to-definition, diagnostics
Third-party extensions from a marketplace; settings sync
Remote development (SSH, containers, WSL, Codespaces in the browser)
Typing latency < 16 ms (one frame); startup in ~1–2 s
A misbehaving extension must not freeze or crash the editor

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: This is a client architecture problem: the constraints are latency per keystroke and isolation from untrusted third-party code, not server QPS.

head: Process
Runs
Why separate
rows: One process per language (TS server, Pyright, rust-analyzer)
CPU-heavy or native work off the UI

blocks.caption: UI talks to everything over IPC/RPC; nothing heavy runs in the renderer

items: LSP is JSON-RPC between an editor (client) and a language server: `textDocument/didOpen`, `didChange` (incremental edits), `completion`, `definition`, `hover`, `publishDiagnostics`.
M editors × N languages becomes M + N implementations.
Servers keep an in-memory model of the workspace (syntax trees, symbol index) and update incrementally on each change.
Requests are cancellable (`$/cancelRequest`) so stale completions from old keystrokes are dropped.
Debug Adapter Protocol (DAP) does the same for debuggers.
Text buffer: a piece tree (VS Code's variant of a piece table) — edits are O(log n) without copying the whole file; handles 100 MB+ files.
Virtualized rendering: only visible lines are in the DOM.
Syntax highlighting with TextMate grammars tokenized incrementally, plus semantic tokens from language servers.
Undo/redo stores edit operations, not snapshots.
Extensions declare **activation events** (onLanguage:python, onCommand) so they load lazily — key to fast startup.
They can't touch the DOM; they use the `vscode` API (commands, providers, webviews) proxied over RPC to the renderer.
Extension host crash → UI shows a message and restarts it; editing continues.
Webviews run in sandboxed iframes with CSP for custom UI.
Workspace Trust: restricted mode for untrusted folders disables code-executing features.
Split: UI runs locally (or in the browser); a **VS Code Server** runs on the remote machine with the extension host, language servers, terminal and file system.
Communication over a single authenticated channel (SSH tunnel / WebSocket); latency-sensitive UI stays local.
Extensions are classified as UI or workspace extensions and run where they belong.
Codespaces = the same server inside a cloud container; github.dev runs a web-only version with a virtual file system.

sections.title: Deep dive: search and settings sync

items: Workspace search shells out to ripgrep, streaming results so the first matches appear instantly; respects .gitignore.
Quick Open uses a fuzzy file index kept up to date by the file watcher.
Settings Sync stores settings, keybindings, extensions and snippets in a cloud service per account, merged with conflict detection.

head: Failure
Impact
Mitigation
rows: Separate extension host; unresponsive-host detection and profiling
Piece tree, virtualization, disable tokenization for giant files, streaming search
Marketplace scanning, publisher verification, Workspace Trust
Reconnect with server kept alive; state on server

items.title: Architecture
items.text: Main, renderer, extension host, language servers.

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: LSP, extension isolation + lazy activation, remote split.

items.q: How would you add real-time pair programming (Live Share)?
items.a: A relay service shares the host's workspace: edits as OT/CRDT ops, cursors as presence, language features proxied from the host.

items.q: How do you keep startup fast with 50 extensions?
items.a: Lazy activation events, cached extension manifests, V8 code cache, deferring non-critical work after first paint.

items.q: How would you build Copilot-style completions?
items.a: Extension collects context (open files, cursor), calls an LLM service with debouncing and cancellation, shows ghost text; caching and rate limits server-side.

items: Multi-process: renderer UI, extension host, language servers.
LSP: JSON-RPC, incremental didChange, cancellable requests.
Piece tree buffer + virtualized rendering.
Lazy activation keeps startup fast.
Remote: UI local, server + extensions remote.
ripgrep streaming search.
